title: Plugin manifest
description: A plugin's committed declaration: what it is, what tools it exposes, and what it may touch. Validated before anything is executed, so an invalid manifest is never run (docs/PLUGIN_SPEC.md 2). An empty filesystem list means no access and an empty network egress list means no network; the manifest is the outer jail and the user's policy may narrow it but never widen it. plugin_api_version is a decimal string rather than a const so a plugin built for a newer API version reaches negotiation and receives PLG-004 naming both versions, instead of failing with a schema error that offers no alternative.

manifest_version.description: Manifest format version, not the plugin's version and not the plugin API version.

plugin_api_version.description: The plugin API version negotiated at handshake. A single decimal number; a valid but unsupported version is refused with PLG-004 rather than a schema failure.

name.description: Globally unique plugin name: two to sixty-four lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.

description.description: One-line description shown by `plugin list` and in approval prompts.

minimum_aicontext_version.description: A SemVer range of aicontext versions this plugin supports. Resolved at install; an unsatisfiable range is refused.

capabilities.description: The tools the plugin implements. A request for a tool not listed here is refused before the plugin is contacted. Tool names must be unique; that cross-field rule is enforced by the SDK and the installer because JSON Schema cannot key on a field.

command.description: The executable the host runs. Never passed through a shell.

args.description: Arguments passed verbatim as an argv array.

tool.description: provider.service.action, exactly three lowercase dot-separated segments.

destructive.description: True forces at least EXPLICIT_APPROVAL regardless of the policy file. A manifest cannot lower the floor its own flag sets.

instructions.description: Human guidance shown at install and in approval prompts. Never a credential value.

name.description: The environment variable or credential-command name. A name, never a value.

read.description: Paths the plugin may read. Empty means none.

write.description: Paths the plugin may write. Empty means none; .ai/ is never implied.

egress.description: Hosts the plugin may contact. Empty means no network.

call_timeout_ms.description: Hard per-call timeout in milliseconds. The runtime may impose a lower cap and fails closed.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on one result in bytes. The runtime kills the process if the cap is exceeded.
